title: 2013 AMC 12A Problem 25
statement: Let \(f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}\) be defined by \(f(z) = z^2 + iz + 1.\) How many complex numbers \(z\) are there such that \(\operatorname{Im}(z) \gt 0\) and both the real and the imaginary parts of \(f(z)\) are integers with absolute value at most \(10?\)

solutions.text:
On the upper half-plane \(H,\) if \(f(z_1) = f(z_2)\) then \((z_1 - z_2)(z_1 + z_2 + i) = 0;\) since \(\operatorname{Im}(z_1), \operatorname{Im}(z_2) \gt 0,\) the factor \(z_1 + z_2 + i \ne 0,\) so \(f\) is one-to-one on \(H.\)

For real \(r,\) the boundary values \(f(r)=r^2+1+ir\) trace the parabola \(\operatorname{Re}(w)=(\operatorname{Im}(w))^2+1.\) Since \(f(i)=-1\) lies to its left and \(f\) is continuous and one-to-one on \(H,\) its image consists precisely of the values \(w\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Re}(w)<(\operatorname{Im}(w))^2+1.\) Thus we count \(w = a + ib\) with \(a, b \in \mathbb{Z},\) \(|a|, |b| \le 10,\) and \(a \lt b^2 + 1:\) \[ \begin{gathered} |S| = 21^2 \\ {}- \sum_{b=-3}^{3}(10 - b^2) \\ = 441 - 42 = 399. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Show \(f\) is one-to-one on the upper half-plane, so counting \(z\) equals counting valid \(f(z)\)
The image is \(\{w : \operatorname{Re}(w) \lt (\operatorname{Im}(w))^2 + 1\};\) count lattice points with \(|\operatorname{Re}|, |\operatorname{Im}| \le 10\)
